data.name: Behrokh
data.gender_notes: Behrokh is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Behrokh is a Persian name that signifies 'bright' or 'radiant'. It is derived from the root 'rokh' which means 'light'. The name is often used to describe someone who is wise, enlightened, or brings joy and happiness to others. The name Behrokh carries the meaning “Bright, Radiant” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Behrokh usually hope their child will grow to embody bright, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Behrokh belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Bright, Radiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Behrokh total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

historical_references.reference: Behrokh was the title given to the vizier of the Seljuk Empire during the reign of Malik Shah I (1072-1092 CE). The title is derived from the Persian word 'bahr', meaning 'ocean' or 'sea', and 'rokh', meaning 'seal'. The vizier was responsible for managing the empire's finances, diplomacy, and military affairs. During his tenure, Behrokh successfully defended the empire against various invasions and expanded its territories.

historical_references.reference: Behrokh was also the name of a Persian poet and scholar who lived during the Safavid Empire (1501-1736 CE). He is known for his works on philosophy, logic, and mathematics, and is considered one of the key figures in the development of Persian philosophy. His most famous work is 'Al-Mabahit al-Mashriqiyya', which is a comprehensive treatise on logic and metaphysics.
